mcu_0160_08007bcc.name: NMI_Handler
mcu_0160_08007bcc.description: Cortex-M NMI vector target. The body is a bare return, so NMI is acknowledged by doing nothing; no clock, watchdog or fault register is touched. Reached only through the vector table, no direct callers.

mcu_0160_08007bce.name: mcu_block200_alloc
mcu_0160_08007bce.summary: Allocate one 200-byte block from the 4088-byte first-fit pool at 0x200027CC
mcu_0160_08007bce.description: Fixed-size 200-byte block allocator. The free list head is the global DAT_2000073C; each free node holds its size in bytes at +0 and the next-node pointer at +4. The first node with size >= 200 is used: an exact 200-byte node is unlinked, a larger node is split and its remainder (size - 200) is re-linked 200 bytes further on. The allocated block's size word is set to 200 and the payload pointer (block + 4) is returned, so the usable payload is 196 bytes. On first use DAT_20000740 is 0, so the pool is initialised as one 0xFF8 (4088) byte node at 0x200027CC and DAT_20000740 is set to 1; afterwards an exhausted pool returns NULL. No locking and no interrupt masking.

returns.description: payload pointer to a 196-byte area, or NULL when no block of 200 bytes is free

mcu_0160_08007bce.notes: The pool's purpose (message or CAN buffers are likely) and the matching free routine are not in this packet. The block size word is written but not read here. Only caller: mcu_0160_08008f34.

mcu_143_08007dc4.name: mcu_timeout_tick_v143
mcu_143_08007dc4.summary: Advance the MCU_143 100-tick timeout counter, decade counter and saturating byte counter
mcu_143_08007dc4.description: Per-call tick of a timeout. Counter DAT_200003AC counts up to 100; on every 10th count the decade counter DAT_20000324 is incremented. At 100 the counter stays saturated, DAT_20001FAA is set to 1 (timeout flag), and the overflow counter DAT_20000326 increments on every further call. Independently, the byte DAT_200003AE increments as a saturating 8-bit counter that stops at 0xFF. The 100-count saturation suggests a heartbeat or message-loss timeout of about 100 ticks (the tick period is not shown in this packet).
mcu_143_08007dc4.notes: Timeout purpose is inferred from the 100-count saturation. The consumer of DAT_20001FAA is outside this packet.

mcu_152_08007e4c.name: mcu_timeout_tick_v152
mcu_152_08007e4c.summary: Advance the MCU_152 100-tick timeout counter and the level field in status halfword 0x20001FCE
mcu_152_08007e4c.description: Same timeout pattern as mcu_timeout_tick_v143 on DAT_200003B0: the counter saturates at 100, the decade counter DAT_20000330 steps every 10 counts, DAT_20001FC2 is set on saturation and the overflow counter DAT_20000332 increments while saturated, and the byte DAT_200003B2 is an 8-bit saturating counter. While saturated, DAT_20000634 counts timed-out ticks up to 0x189C (6300). Bits 9..11 of the status halfword DAT_20001FCE are a 3-bit level: after 300 timed-out ticks the level is forced to 2 (0x400) on every 100th tick unless it already is 2, and the level field is cleared when the 6300 cap is reached. The counter DAT_20000634 is reset to 0 as soon as the timeout counter is below saturation.
mcu_152_08007e4c.notes: The meaning of the level field (escalation of a fault or timeout severity) is inferred from the write pattern only.

mcu_12b_08007ed0.name: mcu_timeout_tick_v12b
mcu_12b_08007ed0.summary: Advance the MCU_12b 100-tick timeout counter and set flag DAT_20001F8A at saturation
mcu_12b_08007ed0.description: Counts DAT_200003B4 up to 100, one step per call. At 100 the counter stays there and the byte DAT_20001F8A is set to 1 on every call. This build has no decade or overflow counter. It is the same timeout pattern as mcu_timeout_tick_v143 and mcu_timeout_tick_v152.
mcu_12b_08007ed0.notes: Consumer of DAT_20001F8A is outside this packet. The 12b build is the only one with DAT_20001F8A.

mcu_12b_08007ef4.name: mcu_setpoint_slew_limit_v12b
mcu_12b_08007ef4.summary: Slew-limit the scaled setpoint into filter DAT_20000F02 and derive output limit DAT_20000F04 (12b)
mcu_12b_08007ef4.description: The raw setpoint DAT_20000EEC is scaled by 20/65536 (x * 0x14 >> 16). The filter state DAT_20000F02 moves toward it: within +-20 counts it steps by 1 per call, beyond that it steps by about one twentieth of the error, and it is clamped to be non-negative. If the mode byte DAT_20000E0B is 1, the output DAT_20000F04 follows the filter until the filter's 10-count bucket, (F02 + 10) / 10, equals DAT_20000DFC >> 15 for 200 consecutive calls (counter DAT_2000062A); then it snaps to DAT_20000DFC scaled by 20/65536. Otherwise a threshold T = 5 x (byte at 0x20001F98 rounded up to even) sets flag DAT_20000628 (T <= DAT_20000F04), and the output follows the filter outside a 10-count band around T, holds T inside the band, and keeps its old value on the lower edge of the band unless DAT_20001F8E >= 195 and T <= output.
mcu_12b_08007ef4.notes: Units of the setpoint and of the mode byte are not established. The decompiler renders the step as a magic-number division by 20 with a sign fix-up, read here as delta/20. The 12b build has its own variant of the 143/152/0160 function mcu_setpoint_slew_limit_std.

mcu_0160_08007f24.name: mcu_setpoint_slew_limit_std
mcu_0160_08007f24.summary: Slew-limit the scaled setpoint into filter DAT_20000F46 and derive output limit DAT_20000F48
mcu_0160_08007f24.description: Same algorithm as mcu_setpoint_slew_limit_v12b with the 143/152/0160 RAM layout: input DAT_20000F30 scaled by 20/65536, filter DAT_20000F46 (+-1 step inside 20 counts, otherwise about delta/20, clamped to >= 0), output DAT_20000F48, mode byte DAT_20000E33 and threshold T = 5 x round-up-even(DAT_20001FDC). When the mode byte is not 1, the output follows the filter 20 or 10 counts above it, holds T inside a 10-count band and uses counter DAT_2000063C (up to 200) as a sustain count on the upper edge. When the mode byte is 1, DAT_2000063A counts how long the filter stays one bucket (200 calls) or two buckets (500 calls) away from DAT_20000E24 >> 15, and the output then snaps to DAT_20000E24 scaled by 20/65536; a filter more than two buckets away resets the count and passes the filter through.
mcu_0160_08007f24.notes: Built for MCU_143, MCU_152 and MCU_0160 (not 12b). Units of DAT_20000F30, DAT_20000E24 and the mode byte are not established. Only caller: mcu_0160_0800a480.

mcu_0160_08008128.name: mcu_pid_update_q15
mcu_0160_08008128.summary: PID-style controller step in Q15 with derivative on measurement and clamped output
mcu_0160_08008128.description: Controller object fields: enable byte +0x3E, gate byte +0x3F, Kp at +0x0C, Ki at +0x10, Kd at +0x14, error-abort threshold at +0x38, output minimum +0x24 and maximum +0x28, integrator +0x30, previous measurement +0x34, saturation status byte +0x3C. The error is e = *(+0x20) - *(+0x18) (reference minus measurement). If disabled it returns 0 and changes nothing. If the gate byte is set and |e| exceeds +0x38 the integrator is cleared and no integral step is taken. The integral step is (Ki*e + 0x4000) >> 15, applied one-sided while the output was saturated high (flag +0x3C or +0x3D equal to 1: only negative steps) or low (equal to 2: only positive steps) - conditional-integration anti-windup. The output is param_2 (feed-forward base) + (Kp*e >> 15) + integrator - (Kd*(meas - previous) >> 15), clamped to [min,max]; +0x3C becomes 1 (high), 2 (low) or 0, the result is written through *(+0x1C) and the measurement is stored at +0x34.

params.name: param_2
params.description: feed-forward base value added to the output

returns.description: 1 if the controller ran, 0 if disabled

mcu_0160_08008128.notes: The algorithm is read directly from the code; the role as a motor or current loop is a guess. Callers mcu_0160_08007364 and mcu_0160_0800772c are outside this packet.

mcu_12b_0800822a.name: mcu_threshold_debounce_update_v12b
mcu_12b_0800822a.summary: Debounce an upper and/or lower threshold with per-side counters and latched trip flags (12b)
mcu_12b_0800822a.description: Control object: upper threshold word at +0x00, lower at +0x04, mode byte at +0x08 (0 = upper only, 1 = lower only, 2 = both), counters at +0x0A (upper) and +0x0C (lower) as halfwords with limits at +0x0E and +0x10, state bytes +0x12 and +0x13, latched flags +0x14 and +0x15. For the upper side, each sample above the threshold increments the counter until it reaches its limit, which latches the trip (+0x12 and +0x14 set to 1); a sample at or below the threshold decrements the counter, and when it is already zero clears +0x12. The lower side works the same with samples below the lower threshold and state bytes +0x13 and +0x15. The function always returns 1.
mcu_12b_0800822a.notes: Only in the 12b build. The thresholds' physical meaning (for example over-current or over-temperature) is not shown here.

mcu_0160_08008260.name: mcu_pid_sync_integrator
mcu_0160_08008260.summary: Reset PID integrator to the clamped current output and latch the current measurement
mcu_0160_08008260.description: Sets the integrator at +0x30 to the present output *(+0x1C) clamped to [+0x24, +0x28], and stores the current measurement *(+0x18) in the previous-measurement slot +0x34. The clamp takes the output as-is if it lies within the limits and otherwise uses the nearer limit. Used to make the controller start from its current output (bumpless transfer), so the derivative term does not see a step at the restart.
mcu_0160_08008260.notes: The bumpless-transfer purpose is inferred. Its caller mcu_0160_080082ac is outside this packet.

mcu_0160_08008282.name: mcu_pid_set_limits
mcu_0160_08008282.summary: Store PID output limits (min < max) and clamp the live output when the loop is enabled
mcu_0160_08008282.description: Accepts the new limits only when min (param_2) is below max (param_3): min is stored at +0x24 and max at +0x28, and 1 is returned. Otherwise nothing changes and 0 is returned. If the enable byte +0x3E is set, the output *(+0x1C) is clamped to [min, max] at once: a value above max becomes max, a value below min becomes min.

returns.description: 1 if the limits were accepted, 0 if min >= max

mcu_0160_08008282.notes: Callers mcu_0160_08003f2c, mcu_0160_08007822 and mcu_0160_08008204 are outside this packet.

mcu_12b_0800829e.name: mcu_threshold_debounce_init_v12b
mcu_12b_0800829e.summary: Initialise a 12b threshold debounce object: thresholds, mode, counter limits, clear state
mcu_12b_0800829e.description: Writes the upper threshold (param_2) at +0x00 and lower threshold (param_3) at +0x04, the upper and lower counter limits (param_4 at +0x0E, param_5 at +0x10) as halfwords, and the mode byte (param_6) at +0x08. The up and down counters at +0x0A and +0x0C, the state and latch bytes +0x12, +0x13, +0x14 and +0x15 are all cleared. Returns 1.

params.name: param_6
params.description: mode: 0 upper only, 1 lower only, 2 both

mcu_12b_0800829e.notes: Only caller in this packet's scope: mcu_12b_08005c80.

mcu_0160_0800833c.name: mcu_pi_update_gain_sched
mcu_0160_0800833c.summary: PI step with speed-scheduled gains (Kp doubled, Ki halved below 0xF0001) and one-sided anti-windup
mcu_0160_0800833c.description: Error e = *(+0x20) - *(+0x18). The divisor g is 2 when DAT_20000F30 < 0xF0001 and 1 otherwise: the proportional gain is Kp*g (Kp at +0x0C) and the integral gain is Ki/g (Ki at +0x10), i.e. gain scheduling on DAT_20000F30. The integrator at +0x30 accumulates (Ki/g * e + 0x4000) >> 15; the step is one-sided while the previous output saturated high (DAT_20000348 set: only negative steps) or low (DAT_20000349 set: only positive steps). The integrator is clamped to [+0x24, +0x28]. The output (Kp*g*e + 0x4000) >> 15 plus the integrator is clamped: above max it writes max and sets DAT_20000348, below min it writes min and sets DAT_20000349, otherwise both flags are cleared. The result goes to *(+0x1C). There is no derivative term and no enable check.

params.name: param_1
params.description: PI object: refs +0x18/+0x20, output ptr +0x1C, Kp +0x0C, Ki +0x10, integrator +0x30, limits +0x24/+0x28

mcu_0160_0800833c.notes: The scheduling interpretation (low-speed gain change) follows from the threshold constant only; DAT_20000F30 units unknown. Only caller: mcu_0160_08003f2c.

mcu_0160_0800844c.name: mcu_threshold_monitor_update_std
mcu_0160_0800844c.summary: Update thresholds and run upper/lower trip monitor with reload counters and hysteresis (143/152/0160)
mcu_0160_0800844c.description: Stores the new thresholds param_3 at +0x00 and param_4 at +0x04. Upper side (mode byte +0x08 equal to 0 or 2): a sample above the upper threshold increments counter A at +0x0A up to its limit at +0x0E; at the limit the trip flag +0x18 and latch +0x1A are set and counter A is reloaded from +0x10. A sample at or below the release level param_5 decrements the counter and clears +0x18 when it is zero. Lower side (mode 1 or 2): a sample below +0x04 increments counter B at +0x0C up to its limit at +0x12; at the limit flag +0x19 and latch +0x1B are set and counter B is reloaded from +0x14. A sample at or above (+0x04 + param_6 hysteresis) decrements counter B and clears +0x19 at zero. Returns 1.
mcu_0160_0800844c.notes: The protected quantity is not identified in this packet. Callers mcu_0160_08005a00 and mcu_0160_08005ab0 are outside this packet.

mcu_0160_080084dc.name: mcu_threshold_monitor_init_std
mcu_0160_080084dc.summary: Initialise the 143/152/0160 threshold monitor object with limits, reload values and mode
mcu_0160_080084dc.description: Writes the mode byte (param_8) at +0x08, thresholds param_2 at +0x00 and param_3 at +0x04, counter A limit param_4 at +0x0E, reload value param_5 at +0x10, counter B limit param_6 at +0x12 and reload value param_7 (word) at +0x14. The counters at +0x0A and +0x0C and the flag and latch bytes +0x18, +0x19, +0x1A and +0x1B are cleared. Returns 1.

params.name: param_8
params.description: mode: 0 upper only, 1 lower only, 2 both

mcu_0160_08008594.name: mcu_pwm_outputs_set_enable
mcu_0160_08008594.summary: Enable or disable the main and complementary outputs of TMR1 channels 1-3 from flag +0x2E5
mcu_0160_08008594.description: Reads-modifies-writes TMR1.CCTRL at 0x40012C20. If the byte at param_1+0x2E5 is non-zero it ORs mask 0x555 (C1EN, C1CEN, C2EN, C2CEN, C3EN, C3CEN, bits 0,2,4,6,8,10), otherwise it ANDs with 0xFFFFFAAA, clearing the same six bits. The polarity bits (C1P, C1CP, C2P, C2CP, C3P, C3CP) and channel-4 bits are left unchanged. This is the output-enable gate for the three motor phases, using the complementary PWM of TMR1.
mcu_0160_08008594.notes: Mapping of the three channels to motor phases is inferred from the three-channel pattern.

mcu_0160_08008968.name: mcu_set_request_flags
mcu_0160_08008968.summary: Set request flags at 0x20001FC9 and 0x20001FCB to 1

mcu_0160_080089a4.name: mcu_callback_slot_dispatch
mcu_0160_080089a4.summary: Call the RAM function pointer in slot 0 or 1 of the two-entry table at 0x20000630

For an index below 2 it loads the pointer at 0x20000630 + index*4 and calls it with no arguments. Indexes 2 and above do nothing. Because the table is in RAM, the handlers are installed at run time by code outside this packet.

mcu_0160_08008c08.name: mcu_msg_ring1_pop
mcu_0160_08008c08.summary: Pop one 5-word record from message ring 1 (32 entries at 0x20001B10, consumer index 0x20001B0C)
mcu_0160_08008c08.description: Ring 1 has 32 records of five 32-bit words (stride 20 bytes) starting at 0x20001B10. The write (producer) index is DAT_20001B08 and the read (consumer) index is DAT_20001B0C. If they differ, the record at the consumer index is copied to the caller's struct (word 0 to +0, word 1 to +4, word 2 to +8, word 3 to +0xC, word 4 to +0x10) and the consumer index is advanced with mask 0x1F. If the ring is empty the caller's struct is left untouched. There is no interrupt masking, so the ring is only safe for one producer and one consumer.

mcu_0160_08008c58.name: mcu_msg_ring2_peek
mcu_0160_08008c58.summary: Copy the head record of message ring 2 without advancing its read index

If the two differ, the record at the read index is copied to the destination: word 0 from 0x20001888, word 1 from 0x2000188C, word 2 from 0x20001890, word 3 from 0x20001894 and word 4 from 0x20001898. Unlike the ring 1 pop, this routine does not advance DAT_20001884, so the caller must do it after use. If the ring is empty the destination is left untouched.

mcu_0160_08008c8c.name: mcu_msg_ring1_push
mcu_0160_08008c8c.summary: Append one 5-word record to message ring 1, dropping it when the ring is full

mcu_0160_08008ea4.name: mcu_read_device_identity

Finally it writes the bitwise NOT of the UID word sum, ~(uid0 + uid1 + uid2), to 0x200003B0. That word is the timeout counter of the MCU_152 build, so the value is used as a seed or check value for the device.

mcu_0160_08008f78.name: mcu_hall_sector_window_update
mcu_0160_08008f78.summary: Set magnitude fault 0x4305 and recompute the expected-sector window bounds at +0x50 and +0x54

The window centre is C = +0x5C + +0x48, where +0x5C is the sector code (k x 0x10C15) produced by mcu_hall_sector_transition. The window depends on the direction state +0x38 (a signed halfword): 0 gives [C-10, C+10]; +1 gives [C-0x860A-f, C+f] (upper bound C+0x860B+f when +0x04 is 0); -1 gives [C-f, C+0x860A+f] (lower bound C-0x860B-f when +0x04 is 0), where f is the fault offset in +0x58. Half a sector is 0x860A, so the window covers about 30 degrees either side of the sector edge.

mcu_0160_08009050.name: mcu_position_multiturn_compute
mcu_0160_08009050.summary: Compute relative position = raw + wraps x 0x6487E - reference, saturated to +-0x7FBC0000
mcu_0160_08009050.description: Computes raw(+0x44) + wraps(+0xA4) x 0x6487E - reference(+0xAC) in 32-bit signed arithmetic. 0x6487E = 411774 = 6 x 0x10C15, which is one electrical revolution when each of the six hall sectors is 0x10C15 counts, so the wrap count +0xA4 counts electrical revolutions. If the result lies within +-0x7FBC0000 it is stored at +0xA8 and returned. Otherwise the saturated value +0x7FBC0000 (positive overflow) or -0x7FBC0000 = 0x80440000 (negative overflow) is stored and returned.

params.name: param_1
params.description: drive context: raw +0x44, wrap count +0xA4, reference +0xAC, result +0xA8

returns.description: relative position in counts, or the saturated +-0x7FBC0000

mcu_0160_08009050.notes: The relation of 0x6487E to the sector step is numerical, confirmed by 6 x 0x10C15 = 0x6487E. The wrap counter is maintained elsewhere, not in this packet. Caller mcu_0160_080031b8 is outside this packet.

mcu_0160_08009094.name: mcu_ctx_flag4_is_clear

mcu_0160_080090a0.name: mcu_hall_sector_transition
mcu_0160_080090a0.summary: Validate a 60-degree hall sector step from +0x5C to +0x60 and set direction +0x38 to +1 or -1
mcu_0160_080090a0.description: Six sector codes are used: 0, 0x10C15, 0x2182A, 0x3243F, 0x43054 and 0x53C69, i.e. k x 0x10C15 for sectors k = 0..5 (60 degrees each, six per electrical revolution). The status byte +0x01 is cleared first. If the current code (+0x5C) is one of the six and the new code (+0x60) is one of its two neighbours mod 6, the direction halfword +0x38 is set to +1 for a step to the lower index (including 0 to 5) and to -1 for a step to the higher index (including 5 to 0), and the status stays 0. An invalid step leaves +0x38 unchanged and stores k+1 (1..6) in the status byte. A current code outside the six leaves the status at 0.

params.name: param_1
params.description: drive context: current sector +0x5C, new sector +0x60, direction +0x38, status byte +0x01

returns.description: 0 for a valid step, 1..6 (k+1 of the current sector) for an invalid step

mcu_0160_080090a0.notes: The hall sensor interpretation is inferred from the six-state, neighbour-only transitions. Callers mcu_0160_08009160 is outside this packet.
